summary: WebSocket-to-SSE proxy downgrade trims final payload leaving partial JSON to client
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using a WebSocket-capable client but routed through an intermediary that rewrites WS->SSE are occasionally receiving truncated final messages. The final SSE event delivered to the browser contains an unterminated JSON payload (missing closing brace and trailing metadata), causing client-side JSON parse failures and aborted UI flows.

Impact:
- NoteStream (enterprise customer) reports repeated "unable to finalize note" errors in their editor for ~6% of long responses (>1024 tokens) originating from our us-east region.
- Client sees partial text, then stream silently ends. No retry is attempted by client SDK because the stream appears closed.

Environment:
- Customer environment: corporate edge that does WS->SSE protocol translation for legacy mobile clients.
- Redwood environment: hosted inference, us-east cluster behind nginx-based edge-proxy fleet with CloudFront in front for some customers.
- Affected model: redwood-chat-13b, streaming mode, SSE transport after downgrade.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure client that attempts WebSocket upgrade but connects through translation proxy that replies with 200 and switches to chunked SSE.
2) Send a generation request that produces >1000 tokens streamed gradually (simulate long completion).
3) Observe final event payload on client and compare to server stream logs.

Observed behavior:
- Server runtime emits full sequence of SSE events, including a final event with metadata and closing JSON object.
- Edge proxy occasionally flushes connection while there's still an incomplete chunk in flight; client receives a partial final JSON (example below) and parsing fails.
- No explicit 5xx returned; connection closed with HTTP/1.1 EOF.

Expected behavior:
- Edge proxy should preserve chunk boundaries and only close the connection after full SSE event has been forwarded. Client should receive a well-formed final JSON and close normally.

Logs / sample truncated payload (from client capture):
{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...final paragraph about deployment best practices"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"meta":{"tokens":1024,"status":"complete"

(Notice missing closing })

Attachments:
- packet capture (pcap) from customer mobile SDK session attached to ticket (sensitive).
- server-side stream trace id: trace-us-east-7b9c
comments: 2026-03-12 - Asha Gupta (reporter): Customer opened after reproducible failures in production. Initial triage shows mismatch between runtime final write and what arrives at client. Requested SRE involvement.

2026-03-12 - Marco Alvarez (assignee): Acknowledged. Spun up a probe harness to replay client flow through our staging proxy farm. Found intermittent truncation when proxy_request_buffering is on and downstream connection gets a keepalive timeout.

2026-03-13 - SRE (investigator): Correlated truncated traces to nginx access logs showing upstream response length smaller than runtime output length for same trace id. Hypothesis: proxy applied an early EOF when reusing backend connection that still had a partially sent chunk in socket buffer.

2026-03-14 - Eng (runtime): Confirmed runtime writes final SSE event in a single write call for long completions. No evidence runtime closed connection early. Working with SRE to test nginx config changes in canary.

2026-03-14 - Support (note): Notified customer about investigation and provided temporary client-side mitigation: enable client fallback to long-poll if SSE message parsing fails, and log the raw payload for support.
investigation_notes: Probe harness: replayed 2000 long streams through edge-proxy pool; truncation observed in ~2.8% of runs when proxy buffering was enabled.

Nginx config: proxy_request_buffering was default (on) for some older edge hosts. When buffering is on, nginx assembles upstream response then streams; on socket reuse race it may prematurely drop trailing buffer fragments on upstream EOF.
Keepalive observations: several edge hosts had keepalive_timeout configured to 30s; long-running streams saw backend connection teardown events that correlate with truncation timestamps.

Workaround test: setting proxy_request_buffering off and proxy_http_version 1.1 reduced truncation to ~0.1% in canary tests. Adding proxy_set_header Connection ''keep-alive'' was beneficial in preventing midstream connection reclaim.

Client-side SDK: current SDK treats any non-terminated JSON as fatal and does not attempt to request missing tail; suggested SDK change to attempt a short re-fetch range when parse fails (debatable due to idempotency).
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied in canary (us-east-edge-c1): proxy_request_buffering disabled, proxy_http_version forced to 1.1, keepalive_timeout increased to 90s. Canary run for 48h shows truncation rate dropped from ~2.8% to 0.08%. Plan: roll config change to remainder of us-east edge hosts today (2026-03-14) and to eu-west next week. Customer notified of temporary client workaround and requested follow-up around metrics. Post-rollout actions: add end-to-end streaming integration test, add an alert for any SSE final-event parse failures exceeding 0.1% of streams, and document proxy recommendations in Confluence.
next_steps: Roll config changes to all us-east edge hosts (owner: Marco Alvarez, target: 2026-03-14)
Monitor trace-us-east-*: ensure truncated payload rate < 0.2% for 72h post-rollout (owner: SRE)
Add a streaming final-event unit test to runtime CI that validates integrity after edge-proxy translation (owner: runtime team)
Follow up with NoteStream on persistent occurrences and provide postmortem if >0.5% recurrence (owner: CS)
Consider SDK resilience change: on parse failure, capture raw tail and optionally request a short re-fetch (action: product + SDK)
public_communication: We drafted a customer-facing note explaining intermittent truncation when intermediaries perform WS->SSE translation and suggested short-term client fallback options. Will publish a KB after rollout completes.
